abstract: Polyhedral integrality guarantees integral stable solutions in several classical stability problems: stable matchings in normal hypergraphs, stable $b$-matchings in unimodular hypergraphs, and kernels in clique-acyclic orientations of perfect graphs. Whether they can be computed efficiently has been a long-standing open question; for kernels in perfect graphs it has been open since the existence theorem of Boros and Gurvich in 1996. We show that, unless $PPAD\subseteq FP$, they cannot. Finding a stable matching is $PPAD$-complete already in linear unimodular hypergraphs with hyperedges of size at most three and vertex degrees at most three. Consequently, finding a kernel in a clique-acyclic orientation of a perfect graph is $PPAD$-hard even if all cliques have at most three vertices, answering an open question of Pass-Lanneau, Igarashi and Meunier, and stable matchings are $PPAD$-hard to find in balanced and in normal hypergraphs. This contrasts with the polynomial algorithm of Chandrasekaran and Kalathur for network hypergraphs. With capacities, even network hypergraphs are hard: University Dual Admission is $PPAD$-complete with capacities at most nine, so stable $b$-matching is $PPAD$-complete on network hypergraphs with hyperedges of size three. This yields $PPAD$-completeness for a natural class of hospitals/residents markets with couples where stable matchings always exist, and $PPAD$-hardness of computing the near-feasible stable matchings, where capacities are flexible. Both reductions are from PURE CIRCUIT with constant-size gadgets. For unit capacities we use a dual-rail encoding, a symmetry-breaking gadget made of two coupled $2\times2$ stable marriage markets, and a parity criterion on the bipartite incidence graph that certifies total unimodularity. We expect these tools to be useful for further hardness results about problems with guaranteed integral solutions.
